description:
HyperFlood - The Hyper Local Flood Early Warning System

HyperFlood is a web-based Hyper Local flood early warning system developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!” It investigates how Earth-system variables such as precipitation and temperature have changed over time using NASA data, and connects these historical trends with present-day environmental conditions.
summary:
HyperFlood is a web-based Hyper Local flood early warning system developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!” It investigates how Earth-system variables such as precipitation and temperature have changed over time using NASA data, and connects these historical trends with present-day environmental conditions.

Users can select any location on the map to explore NASA historical trends alongside elevation and terrain, soil wetness and runoff potential, rivers and drainage, and recent rainfall. By connecting changes across multiple parts of the Earth system, HyperFlood transforms complex environmental data into simple, explainable insights that help people understand how changing conditions may contribute to local flood vulnerability.
details:
HyperFlood is a web-based flood intelligence platform that combines NASA satellite data, geographical information and weather forecasts to assess local flood vulnerability. It analyses historical rainfall, soil moisture, elevation, nearby waterways and forecast precipitation using NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, MERRA-2, Copernicus DEM, OpenStreetMap and Open-Meteo. Developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, it is hosted on GitHub Pages.

Its innovative Past–Present–Future approach combines historical trends, current geographical conditions and future rainfall to identify potential flood threats. HyperFlood aims to improve flood awareness, identify vulnerable areas and support disaster preparedness. The project considers terrain, soil conditions, rainfall patterns, data accuracy and satellite limitations, demonstrating how NASA Earth observation resources can support accessible, location-specific flood intelligence.

Data Sources and Their Purpose:

  • NASA POWER: Historical rainfall and temperature trends to understand long-term environmental patterns.
  • NASA GPM IMERG: Satellite-based precipitation estimates to analyse rainfall intensity and distribution.
  • NASA MERRA-2: Historical atmospheric and soil moisture data to assess environmental and ground wetness conditions.
  • Copernicus DEM GLO-90: Elevation and terrain data to identify low-lying areas and drainage patterns.
  • OpenStreetMap / Overpass API: River, stream and canal locations to assess proximity to waterways.
  • Open-Meteo: Weather forecasts and future precipitation to evaluate potential rainfall-related flood threats.
